enums.name: TaskType

values.name: Classification
values.doc:
Classification in machine learning and statistics is a supervised learning approach in which
the computer program learns from the data given to it and make new observations or classifications.

values.name: Regression
values.doc: Regression means to predict the value using the input data. Regression models are used to predict a continuous value.

values.name: Forecasting
values.doc:
Forecasting is a special kind of regression task that deals with time-series data and creates forecasting model
that can be used to predict the near future values based on the inputs.

values.name: ImageClassification
values.doc:
Image Classification. Multi-class image classification is used when an image is classified with only a single label
from a set of classes - e.g. each image is classified as either an image of a 'cat' or a 'dog' or a 'duck'.

values.name: ImageClassificationMultilabel
values.doc:
Image Classification Multilabel. Multi-label image classification is used when an image could have one or more labels
from a set of labels - e.g. an image could be labeled with both 'cat' and 'dog'.

values.name: ImageObjectDetection
values.doc:
Image Object Detection. Object detection is used to identify objects in an image and locate each object with a
bounding box e.g. locate all dogs and cats in an image and draw a bounding box around each.

values.name: ImageInstanceSegmentation
values.doc:
Image Instance Segmentation. Instance segmentation is used to identify objects in an image at the pixel level,
drawing a polygon around each object in the image.

values.name: TextClassification
values.doc:
Text classification (also known as text tagging or text categorization) is the process of sorting texts into categories.
Categories are mutually exclusive.

values.name: TextClassificationMultilabel
values.doc: Multilabel classification task assigns each sample to a group (zero or more) of target labels.

values.name: TextNER
values.doc:
Text Named Entity Recognition a.k.a. TextNER.
Named Entity Recognition (NER) is the ability to take free-form text and identify the occurrences of entities such as people, locations, organizations, and more.

values.name: TfIdf
values.doc: Tf-Idf stands for, term-frequency times inverse document-frequency. This is a common term weighting scheme for identifying information from documents.

values.name: WoETargetEncoder
values.doc: Weight of Evidence encoding is a technique used to encode categorical variables. It uses the natural log of the P(1)/P(0) to create weights.

values.name: LabelEncoder
values.doc: Label encoder converts labels/categorical variables in a numerical form.

values.name: WordEmbedding
values.doc: Word embedding helps represents words or phrases as a vector, or a series of numbers.

values.name: NaiveBayes
values.doc: Naive Bayes is a classified that is used for classification of discrete features that are categorically distributed.

values.name: CountVectorizer

values.name: HashOneHotEncoder

enums.name: ClassificationPrimaryMetric

values.name: AUCWeighted
values.doc:
AUC is the Area under the curve.
This metric represents arithmetic mean of the score for each class,
weighted by the number of true instances in each class.

values.name: Accuracy
values.doc: Accuracy is the ratio of predictions that exactly match the true class labels.

values.name: NormMacroRecall
values.doc:
Normalized macro recall is recall macro-averaged and normalized, so that random
performance has a score of 0, and perfect performance has a score of 1.

values.name: AveragePrecisionScoreWeighted
values.doc:
The arithmetic mean of the average precision score for each class, weighted by
the number of true instances in each class.

values.name: PrecisionScoreWeighted
values.doc: The arithmetic mean of precision for each class, weighted by number of true instances in each class.

enums.doc: Primary metrics for classification tasks.

enums.name: ClassificationModel

values.name: LogisticRegression
values.doc:
Logistic regression is a fundamental classification technique.
It belongs to the group of linear classifiers and is somewhat similar to polynomial and linear regression.
Logistic regression is fast and relatively uncomplicated, and it's convenient for you to interpret the results.
Although it's essentially a method for binary classification, it can also be applied to multiclass problems.

values.name: SGD
values.doc:
SGD: Stochastic gradient descent is an optimization algorithm often used in machine learning applications
to find the model parameters that correspond to the best fit between predicted and actual outputs.

values.name: MultinomialNaiveBayes
values.doc:
The multinomial Naive Bayes classifier is suitable for classification with discrete features (e.g., word counts for text classification).
The multinomial distribution normally requires integer feature counts. However, in practice, fractional counts such as tf-idf may also work.

values.name: BernoulliNaiveBayes
values.doc: Naive Bayes classifier for multivariate Bernoulli models.

values.name: SVM
values.doc:
A support vector machine (SVM) is a supervised machine learning model that uses classification algorithms for two-group classification problems.
After giving an SVM model sets of labeled training data for each category, they're able to categorize new text.

values.name: LinearSVM
values.doc:
A support vector machine (SVM) is a supervised machine learning model that uses classification algorithms for two-group classification problems.
After giving an SVM model sets of labeled training data for each category, they're able to categorize new text.
Linear SVM performs best when input data is linear, i.e., data can be easily classified by drawing the straight line between classified values on a plotted graph.

values.name: KNN
values.doc:
K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm uses 'feature similarity' to predict the values of new datapoints
which further means that the new data point will be assigned a value based on how closely it matches the points in the training set.

values.name: DecisionTree
values.doc:
Decision Trees are a non-parametric supervised learning method used for both classification and regression tasks.
The goal is to create a model that predicts the value of a target variable by learning simple decision rules inferred from the data features.

values.name: RandomForest
values.doc:
Random forest is a supervised learning algorithm.
The "forest" it builds, is an ensemble of decision trees, usually trained with the "bagging" method.
The general idea of the bagging method is that a combination of learning models increases the overall result.

values.name: ExtremeRandomTrees
values.doc: Extreme Trees is an ensemble machine learning algorithm that combines the predictions from many decision trees. It is related to the widely used random forest algorithm.

values.name: LightGBM
values.doc: LightGBM is a gradient boosting framework that uses tree based learning algorithms.

values.name: GradientBoosting
values.doc: The technique of transiting week learners into a strong learner is called Boosting. The gradient boosting algorithm process works on this theory of execution.

values.name: XGBoostClassifier
values.doc: XGBoost: Extreme Gradient Boosting Algorithm. This algorithm is used for structured data where target column values can be divided into distinct class values.

enums.doc: Enum for all classification models supported by AutoML.

enums.name: ForecastingModel

values.name: AutoArima
values.doc:
Auto-Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model uses time-series data and statistical analysis to interpret the data and make future predictions.
This model aims to explain data by using time series data on its past values and uses linear regression to make predictions.

values.name: Prophet
values.doc:
Prophet is a procedure for forecasting time series data based on an additive model where non-linear trends are fit with yearly, weekly, and daily seasonality, plus holiday effects.
It works best with time series that have strong seasonal effects and several seasons of historical data. Prophet is robust to missing data and shifts in the trend, and typically handles outliers well.

values.name: Naive
values.doc: The Naive forecasting model makes predictions by carrying forward the latest target value for each time-series in the training data.

values.name: SeasonalNaive
values.doc: The Seasonal Naive forecasting model makes predictions by carrying forward the latest season of target values for each time-series in the training data.

values.name: Average
values.doc: The Average forecasting model makes predictions by carrying forward the average of the target values for each time-series in the training data.

values.name: SeasonalAverage
values.doc: The Seasonal Average forecasting model makes predictions by carrying forward the average value of the latest season of data for each time-series in the training data.

values.name: ExponentialSmoothing
values.doc: Exponential smoothing is a time series forecasting method for univariate data that can be extended to support data with a systematic trend or seasonal component.

values.name: Arimax
values.doc:
An Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Explanatory Variable (ARIMAX) model can be viewed as a multiple regression model with one or more autoregressive (AR) terms and/or one or more moving average (MA) terms.
This method is suitable for forecasting when data is stationary/non stationary, and multivariate with any type of data pattern, i.e., level/trend /seasonality/cyclicity.

values.name: TCNForecaster

values.name: ElasticNet
values.doc: Elastic net is a popular type of regularized linear regression that combines two popular penalties, specifically the L1 and L2 penalty functions.

values.name: GradientBoosting
values.doc: The technique of transiting week learners into a strong learner is called Boosting. The gradient boosting algorithm process works on this theory of execution.

values.name: DecisionTree
values.doc:
Decision Trees are a non-parametric supervised learning method used for both classification and regression tasks.
The goal is to create a model that predicts the value of a target variable by learning simple decision rules inferred from the data features.

values.name: KNN
values.doc:
K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm uses 'feature similarity' to predict the values of new datapoints
which further means that the new data point will be assigned a value based on how closely it matches the points in the training set.

values.name: LassoLars
values.doc: Lasso model fit with Least Angle Regression a.k.a. Lars. It is a Linear Model trained with an L1 prior as regularizer.

values.name: SGD
values.doc:
SGD: Stochastic gradient descent is an optimization algorithm often used in machine learning applications
to find the model parameters that correspond to the best fit between predicted and actual outputs.
It's an inexact but powerful technique.

values.name: RandomForest
values.doc:
Random forest is a supervised learning algorithm.
The "forest" it builds, is an ensemble of decision trees, usually trained with the "bagging" method.
The general idea of the bagging method is that a combination of learning models increases the overall result.

values.name: ExtremeRandomTrees
values.doc: Extreme Trees is an ensemble machine learning algorithm that combines the predictions from many decision trees. It is related to the widely used random forest algorithm.

values.name: LightGBM
values.doc: LightGBM is a gradient boosting framework that uses tree based learning algorithms.

values.name: XGBoostRegressor

properties.name: errorThreshold
properties.doc:
Error threshold, if the error count for the entire input goes above this value,
the batch inference will be aborted. Range is [-1, int.MaxValue].
For FileDataset, this value is the count of file failures.
For TabularDataset, this value is the count of record failures.
If set to -1 (the lower bound), all failures during batch inference will be ignored.

properties.name: loggingLevel
properties.doc:
Log verbosity for batch inferencing.
Increasing verbosity order for logging is : Warning, Info and Debug.
The default value is Info.

properties.name: maxConcurrencyPerInstance

properties.name: miniBatchSize
properties.doc:
Size of the mini-batch passed to each batch invocation.
For FileDataset, this is the number of files per mini-batch.
For TabularDataset, this is the size of the records in bytes, per mini-batch.

properties.doc:
[Required] The collection configuration. Each collection has it own configuration to collect model data and the name of collection can be arbitrary string.
Model data collector can be used for either payload logging or custom logging or both of them. Collection request and response are reserved for payload logging, others are for custom logging.

properties.doc: Enable or disable data collection.

properties.name: dataId
properties.doc: The data asset arm resource id. Client side will ensure data asset is pointing to the blob storage, and backend will collect data to the blob storage.

properties.name: samplingRate
properties.doc: The sampling rate for collection. Sampling rate 1.0 means we collect 100% of data by default.

properties.name: requestLogging
properties.doc: The request logging configuration for mdc, it includes advanced logging settings for all collections. It's optional.

properties.name: captureHeaders
properties.doc: For payload logging, we only collect payload by default. If customers also want to collect the specified headers, they can set them in captureHeaders so that backend will collect those headers along with payload.

properties.name: rollingRate
properties.doc:
When model data is collected to blob storage, we need to roll the data to different path to avoid logging all of them in a single blob file.
If the rolling rate is hour, all data will be collected in the blob path /yyyy/MM/dd/HH/.
If it's day, all data will be collected in blob path /yyyy/MM/dd/.
The other benefit of rolling path is that model monitoring ui is able to select a time range of data very quickly.

values.doc:
Classification in machine learning and statistics is a supervised learning approach in which
the computer program learns from the data given to it and make new observations or classifications.
values.name: Classification

values.doc: Regression means to predict the value using the input data. Regression models are used to predict a continuous value.
values.name: Regression

values.doc:
Forecasting is a special kind of regression task that deals with time-series data and creates forecasting model
that can be used to predict the near future values based on the inputs.
values.name: Forecasting

values.doc:
Image Classification. Multi-class image classification is used when an image is classified with only a single label
from a set of classes - e.g. each image is classified as either an image of a 'cat' or a 'dog' or a 'duck'.
values.name: ImageClassification

values.doc:
Image Classification Multilabel. Multi-label image classification is used when an image could have one or more labels
from a set of labels - e.g. an image could be labeled with both 'cat' and 'dog'.
values.name: ImageClassificationMultilabel

values.doc:
Image Object Detection. Object detection is used to identify objects in an image and locate each object with a
bounding box e.g. locate all dogs and cats in an image and draw a bounding box around each.
values.name: ImageObjectDetection

values.doc:
Image Instance Segmentation. Instance segmentation is used to identify objects in an image at the pixel level,
drawing a polygon around each object in the image.
values.name: ImageInstanceSegmentation

values.doc:
Text classification (also known as text tagging or text categorization) is the process of sorting texts into categories.
Categories are mutually exclusive.
values.name: TextClassification

values.doc: Multilabel classification task assigns each sample to a group (zero or more) of target labels.
values.name: TextClassificationMultilabel

values.doc:
Text Named Entity Recognition a.k.a. TextNER.
Named Entity Recognition (NER) is the ability to take free-form text and identify the occurrences of entities such as people, locations, organizations, and more.
values.name: TextNER

valueType.doc: Enum for all classification models supported by AutoML.

values.doc:
Logistic regression is a fundamental classification technique.
It belongs to the group of linear classifiers and is somewhat similar to polynomial and linear regression.
Logistic regression is fast and relatively uncomplicated, and it's convenient for you to interpret the results.
Although it's essentially a method for binary classification, it can also be applied to multiclass problems.
values.name: LogisticRegression

values.doc:
SGD: Stochastic gradient descent is an optimization algorithm often used in machine learning applications
to find the model parameters that correspond to the best fit between predicted and actual outputs.
values.name: SGD

values.doc:
The multinomial Naive Bayes classifier is suitable for classification with discrete features (e.g., word counts for text classification).
The multinomial distribution normally requires integer feature counts. However, in practice, fractional counts such as tf-idf may also work.
values.name: MultinomialNaiveBayes

values.doc: Naive Bayes classifier for multivariate Bernoulli models.
values.name: BernoulliNaiveBayes

values.doc:
A support vector machine (SVM) is a supervised machine learning model that uses classification algorithms for two-group classification problems.
After giving an SVM model sets of labeled training data for each category, they're able to categorize new text.
values.name: SVM

values.doc:
A support vector machine (SVM) is a supervised machine learning model that uses classification algorithms for two-group classification problems.
After giving an SVM model sets of labeled training data for each category, they're able to categorize new text.
Linear SVM performs best when input data is linear, i.e., data can be easily classified by drawing the straight line between classified values on a plotted graph.
values.name: LinearSVM

values.doc:
K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm uses 'feature similarity' to predict the values of new datapoints
which further means that the new data point will be assigned a value based on how closely it matches the points in the training set.
values.name: KNN

values.doc:
Decision Trees are a non-parametric supervised learning method used for both classification and regression tasks.
The goal is to create a model that predicts the value of a target variable by learning simple decision rules inferred from the data features.
values.name: DecisionTree

values.doc:
Random forest is a supervised learning algorithm.
The "forest" it builds, is an ensemble of decision trees, usually trained with the "bagging" method.
The general idea of the bagging method is that a combination of learning models increases the overall result.
values.name: RandomForest

values.doc: Extreme Trees is an ensemble machine learning algorithm that combines the predictions from many decision trees. It is related to the widely used random forest algorithm.
values.name: ExtremeRandomTrees

values.doc: LightGBM is a gradient boosting framework that uses tree based learning algorithms.
values.name: LightGBM

values.doc: The technique of transiting week learners into a strong learner is called Boosting. The gradient boosting algorithm process works on this theory of execution.
values.name: GradientBoosting

values.doc: XGBoost: Extreme Gradient Boosting Algorithm. This algorithm is used for structured data where target column values can be divided into distinct class values.
values.name: XGBoostClassifier

values.doc:
Auto-Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model uses time-series data and statistical analysis to interpret the data and make future predictions.
This model aims to explain data by using time series data on its past values and uses linear regression to make predictions.
values.name: AutoArima

values.doc:
Prophet is a procedure for forecasting time series data based on an additive model where non-linear trends are fit with yearly, weekly, and daily seasonality, plus holiday effects.
It works best with time series that have strong seasonal effects and several seasons of historical data. Prophet is robust to missing data and shifts in the trend, and typically handles outliers well.
values.name: Prophet

values.doc: The Naive forecasting model makes predictions by carrying forward the latest target value for each time-series in the training data.
values.name: Naive

values.doc: The Seasonal Naive forecasting model makes predictions by carrying forward the latest season of target values for each time-series in the training data.
values.name: SeasonalNaive

values.doc: The Average forecasting model makes predictions by carrying forward the average of the target values for each time-series in the training data.
values.name: Average

values.doc: The Seasonal Average forecasting model makes predictions by carrying forward the average value of the latest season of data for each time-series in the training data.
values.name: SeasonalAverage

values.doc: Exponential smoothing is a time series forecasting method for univariate data that can be extended to support data with a systematic trend or seasonal component.
values.name: ExponentialSmoothing

values.doc:
An Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Explanatory Variable (ARIMAX) model can be viewed as a multiple regression model with one or more autoregressive (AR) terms and/or one or more moving average (MA) terms.
This method is suitable for forecasting when data is stationary/non stationary, and multivariate with any type of data pattern, i.e., level/trend /seasonality/cyclicity.
values.name: Arimax

values.doc: TCNForecaster: Temporal Convolutional Networks Forecaster. //TODO: Ask forecasting team for brief intro.
values.name: TCNForecaster

values.doc: Elastic net is a popular type of regularized linear regression that combines two popular penalties, specifically the L1 and L2 penalty functions.
values.name: ElasticNet

values.doc: The technique of transiting week learners into a strong learner is called Boosting. The gradient boosting algorithm process works on this theory of execution.
values.name: GradientBoosting

values.doc:
Decision Trees are a non-parametric supervised learning method used for both classification and regression tasks.
The goal is to create a model that predicts the value of a target variable by learning simple decision rules inferred from the data features.
values.name: DecisionTree

values.doc:
K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm uses 'feature similarity' to predict the values of new datapoints
which further means that the new data point will be assigned a value based on how closely it matches the points in the training set.
values.name: KNN

values.doc: Lasso model fit with Least Angle Regression a.k.a. Lars. It is a Linear Model trained with an L1 prior as regularizer.
values.name: LassoLars

values.doc:
SGD: Stochastic gradient descent is an optimization algorithm often used in machine learning applications
to find the model parameters that correspond to the best fit between predicted and actual outputs.
It's an inexact but powerful technique.
values.name: SGD

values.doc:
Random forest is a supervised learning algorithm.
The "forest" it builds, is an ensemble of decision trees, usually trained with the "bagging" method.
The general idea of the bagging method is that a combination of learning models increases the overall result.
values.name: RandomForest

values.doc: Extreme Trees is an ensemble machine learning algorithm that combines the predictions from many decision trees. It is related to the widely used random forest algorithm.
values.name: ExtremeRandomTrees

values.doc: LightGBM is a gradient boosting framework that uses tree based learning algorithms.
values.name: LightGBM

values.doc: XGBoostRegressor: Extreme Gradient Boosting Regressor is a supervised machine learning model using ensemble of base learners.
values.name: XGBoostRegressor

methods.name: GetPrivateLinkResources
methods.doc:
Called by Client (Portal, CLI, etc) to get available "private link resources" for the workspace.
Each "private link resource" is a connection endpoint (IP address) to the resource.
Pre single connection endpoint per workspace: the Data Plane IP address, returned by DNS resolution.
Other RPs, such as Azure Storage, have multiple - one for Blobs, other for Queues, etc.
Defined in the "[NRP] Private Endpoint Design" doc, topic "GET API for GroupIds".
